data.title: CTA
data.tagline: Tell visitors the next action you want them to take
data.description: A call to action turns the page's message into a concrete next step, such as Start free, Book a demo, or Download. The wording should describe the result, and the action should appear after enough context to make the choice reasonable.

use: Continue after the page has explained the value
avoid: Label every button as a call to action
Use vague text such as Submit when the result matters
Repeat a high-pressure action before giving context
Offer several equal actions that lead in different directions

lessonPractice.title: A landing page primarily wants visitors to start a free trial, but its hero has equally prominent Submit, Learn more, and Contact us buttons. What should change?

options.label: Emphasize Start free trial, demote the other paths, and state the trial conditions
options.feedback: The primary action names its outcome, while hierarchy and relevant conditions reduce hesitation at the key step.

options.label: Keep three equally prominent primary buttons and let each visitor decide
options.feedback: Multiple primary goals compete within one visual region, making the intended next step harder to identify.

options.label: Rename every button Submit and explain the result only after it is clicked
options.feedback: Submit does not say whether it starts a trial, reveals information, or contacts sales, so the outcome is unclear beforehand.

data.agentPrompt: Make Start free trial the single primary hero CTA and state the duration, price, and credit-card requirement nearby. Demote Learn more and Contact us to secondary paths, then verify that the post-click result matches the promise.
